Calculate Gaussian reference MSE, its decomposition, and a bound

Source: R/gaussian.R
gaussian_cv.Rd

Assumes jointly Gaussian responses with known mean and the supplied stationary covariance, fixed locations, folds and target weights. Prediction uses all available observations. Target observations have fresh independent noise even when their coordinates coincide with training locations. The calculation averages over repeated response datasets; it is not an observed CV score.

Usage

gaussian_cv(locations, folds, target, covariance)

Arguments

locations

Numeric two-column coordinates or projected spatial points.

folds

A partition accepted by cv_folds().

target

A prediction_target() or target coordinates.

covariance

A spatial_covariance() object. A correlation function alone is insufficient because the calculation requires total variance.

Value

A spcv_gaussian list with scalar target_mse, cv_mse, optimism, J2, one_neighbour, additional_neighbours, lower, upper, and estimated_covariance; and location-level validation and target data frames of MSE reductions and bounds. Costs are cubic in training-set size.

Details

optimism is target MSE minus expected CV MSE. It equals one_neighbour (total variance times J2) plus additional_neighbours. The latter is the validation-minus-target difference in the extra MSE reduction supplied by observations beyond the nearest. With strictly positive nugget, lower and upper bound optimism using conditional covariance residuals. These are deterministic limits under the supplied model, not confidence intervals. Bounds are NA when the nugget is zero. Supplying estimated covariance gives a plug-in model calculation, not a guarantee about actual CV bias.

Examples

xy <- cbind(c(-1, 0, 1), 0)
q <- prediction_target(matrix(c(2, 0), nrow = 1))
result <- gaussian_cv(xy, 1:3, q, spatial_covariance(1, 0.8))
result
#> Gaussian reference calculation
#>            target_mse                cv_mse              optimism 
#>           0.912868743           0.889812660           0.023056082 
#>         one_neighbour additional_neighbours                 lower 
#>           0.000000000           0.023056082          -0.002661682 
#>                 upper 
#>           0.116354041 
# Identical nearest distances, but full-neighbour optimism is about 0.02306.
